items.text: I understand the difference between archiving (bundling) and compression (size reduction)
I can create a TAR archive using tar -cvf and explain each flag
I can extract files from a TAR archive using tar -xvf
I can view archive contents without extracting using tar -tvf
I can compress a TAR archive with gzip and decompress with gunzip
I understand ZIP does both archiving and compression in one step
I can explain what a VPC is and why it is scoped to one Region
I can explain the difference between a public and a private subnet
I understand the Internet Gateway's role and the one-per-VPC limit
I can explain how a Route Table makes a subnet public (0.0.0.0/0 → IGW)
I understand NACL — stateless, subnet-level, numbered rules, allow and deny
I understand Security Groups — stateful, instance-level, allow-only rules
I can explain the NACL vs Security Group difference in an interview
I can name all 6 core networking components and their purpose from memory
I know NACL is stateless and Security Group is stateful
I know why NACL needs outbound rules for ephemeral ports (1024-65535)
I can trace a request from the internet to an EC2 instance through all 5 checkpoints
I know Security Groups cannot have DENY rules but NACLs can
